summary: PAPER-HE-18 is a careful and heavily repaired extraction of He's Cocenters of p-adic groups I. It has 123 items, 7 routes and 13 source issues. Its library items check out at the pins, its twisted-commutator and Ω-transport repairs re-derive, and 12 of its 13 source issues hold. There are 10 findings: 6 medium and 4 low. (1) The Kottwitz homomorphism on G itself (G → G/G_0 ≅ Ω, θ-equivariant) has no item, although Theorem 3's disjointness and the proof of Theorem 23 use it; N8's step 'Distinct κ cannot intersect' rests on nothing. (2) A missed error in the proof of Theorem 23, independent of the coefficient ring: G^rig_0 = {κ(g) ∈ Ω_0} is not stable under twisted conjugation, so H̄^rig = (H̄^rig)_0 ⊕ (H̄^rig)_1 fails (PGL_3 with its outer automorphism, f = 1_I). The existence of the finite set A is also unargued. E2's reason relies on this truncation. (3) E3's correction, confirmed by the review, says a Noetherian ring restores Theorem 20. It does not: over R = F_3[x,z]/(xz,z^2) with G = Q_2^×, the restriction needs 2 generators, not N_ν[I:I_n] = 1. (4) Straight elements and the straight-class classification have three owners: HE-18 → Root-systems Part II, Kisin–Zhou 25 → BunGAndNewtonStrata, van Hoften 24 → ADLV Part II. (5) The cocenter and invariant distributions of C_c(G) are planned both in the NewtonCocenters Part II and in SmoothRepresentationsCharactersPartII (HKW22, Hansen 26: Kazhdan density, trace Paley–Wiener), with no owner named. (6) The library audit missed the double-coset Hecke ring at the pins (Mathlib HeckeRing, Tau Ceti HeckeCosetModule.mul, instRingHeckeRing, mul_single_single_of_mulMap_eq), which is H6's carrier and L10's combinatorial core. Low: (7) E8 wrongly confines the lattice error to non-quasi-split groups (unramified U(1) gives Z/2 against 0). (8) There is no sourceVersions field, so collation files the paper as preprint-only. (9) A3 overclaims 'planned' at RG2.3, where Fintzen 21 and GHS 24 mark the Moy–Prasad filtration missing. (10) G5's gap, Remark 8's untwisted '·' and E1's §0.6 locator are missing from the source-issue record.

findings.where: PAPER-HE-18/N8 (proofStep 'Distinct κ cannot intersect'), N1, R16/R2; route 7 (SmoothRepresentationsPartIINewtonCocenters) and route 4 (RG2.4); no item
findings.claim: The Kottwitz homomorphism on the group itself, kappa_G : G -> Omega = W~/W_a (equivalently G/G_0, where G_0 is the subgroup generated by the parahorics), has no item. The paper uses it twice. (i) The first step of the disjointness proof of Theorem 3: 'It is easy to see that if nu_1 and nu_2 have different Omega_theta-factor, then G(nu_1) ∩ G(nu_2) = ∅.' This needs a function on G that is constant on each IẇI with value kappa(w), and whose image in Omega_theta = Omega/(1 - theta)Omega is invariant under theta-twisted conjugation. That is: G_0 is normal and theta-stable, G/G_0 ≅ N/N_0 ≅ Omega by the Bruhat decomposition, and kappa_G(h g theta(h)^-1) = kappa_G(g) + (1 - theta)kappa_G(h). (ii) The proof of Theorem 23 defines G^rig_0 = {g ∈ G^rig ; kappa(g) ∈ Omega_0}, which is kappa on G, not on W~. Item C1 defines kappa only on W~ (its api He18.kottwitzTwisted is kappa(x w theta(x)^-1) = kappa(w) for x in W~), and A7 constructs only the double Tits system. N8's proof step 'Distinct κ cannot intersect' therefore rests on nothing any item provides, and N8's prerequisites (N5, C9, N3, N7) do not supply it. The Kottwitz map kappa_G : G(F-breve) -> pi_1(G)_I and its B(G) version are planned at BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG1 ('Construct pi_1(G), its Galois coinvariants, the Kottwitz map kappa'). But this paper needs only the elementary F-rational form G -> G/G_0 ≅ Omega together with its theta-equivariance, and that follows from A5 and A7. (Disclosure: this session's PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21 routes the B(G) Kottwitz map to BG1, and RT-PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-18/10 asked for kappa_G items citing BG1.)

Proof of Theorem 23, p. 25: 'Let G^rig_0 = {g ∈ G^rig ; κ(g) ∈ Ω0} and G^rig_1 = G^rig − G^rig_0.' §1.1, p. 6: 'Let G_0 be the subgroup of G generated by all parahoric subgroups, and define N_0 A = G_0 ∩ N_G A(F) ... W̃ = W_a ⋊ Ω'. Item C1: 'define Ω_θ=Ω/(1−θ)Ω and κ(w) as the image of w in Ω_θ', api 'κ(xwθ(x)⁻¹)=κ(w)' (for x in W̃). Item N8 proofSteps: 'N5 supplies coverage. Distinct κ cannot intersect; reduce equal κ to standard triples, then apply N7.' A search of all 123 items for kappa or G_0 applied to elements of G finds only A7's 'Let G0 be generated by parahoric subgroups and N0=G0∩N_G(A)(F)'. BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG1 stage text (research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/BunGAndNewtonStrata.json): 'Construct pi_1(G), its Galois coinvariants, the Kottwitz map kappa and rational dominant Newton cocharacter nu.'
findings.fix: Add an item (construction/theorem, route 4, ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.4, or route 7 if the maintainer prefers) with this statement. For the local datum, G_0 is a normal, theta-stable subgroup and G = ⊔_{τ∈Ω} G_0 τ̇, so there is a surjective homomorphism kappa_G : G -> Omega with kernel G_0. Its properties: kappa_G(IẇI) = pr_Omega(w); kappa_G ∘ theta = theta ∘ kappa_G; kappa_G(h g theta(h)^-1) = kappa_G(g) + (1 - theta)kappa_G(h); hence the composite G -> Omega_theta is constant on theta-twisted classes and equals the first coordinate of nu on G(nu). Cite BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG1 only for the identification Omega ≅ pi_1(G)_I^sigma (Haines-Rapoport), which this paper does not need. Make it a prerequisite of N8 (and of any rigid-part splitting used by R16), and replace N8's proof step by 'kappa_G separates strata with different Omega_theta-factor'.

findings.where: PAPER-HE-18 sourceIssues (none records it; E2's reason relies on it; E6 covers only the coefficient ring), proof of Theorem 23, pp. 24-25
findings.claim: The proof of Theorem 23 has a false step that no source issue records, and it holds even over a field. After truncating to Omega_0 = <theta>·Omega' (theta-stable and finite), the paper asserts that H̄^rig = (H̄^rig)_0 ⊕ (H̄^rig)_1 and J(G)^rig = J(G)^rig_0 ⊕ J(G)^rig_1, where G^rig_0 = {g ∈ G^rig : kappa(g) ∈ Omega_0}. This needs G^rig_0 to be stable under theta-twisted conjugation. But kappa(h g theta(h)^-1) = kappa(g) + (1 - theta)kappa(h), so stability needs Omega_0 to be a union of cosets of (1 - theta)Omega; theta-stability does not give that. Counterexample inside the paper's hypotheses: G = PGL_3(F), theta(g) = J·(g^T)^-1·J^-1 with J antidiagonal (it preserves the diagonal torus and the standard Iwahori, and acts on Omega = Z/3 by -1), and omega = 1, R = C. Take f = 1_I, so Omega' = Omega_0 = {0}, and h = τ̇ a length-zero generator. Then ^h f = 1_{τ̇θ(τ̇)^-1 I} is supported where kappa = 1 - (-1) = 2 ≠ 0, so [f] = [^h f] lies in both (H̄^rig)_0 and (H̄^rig)_1. It is nonzero, because j(f) = ∫_G f dμ is a (theta,1)-invariant distribution with j(1_I) = μ(I) ≠ 0. So the displayed direct sums fail, and so do 'J(G)^rig_0 = (H̄^rig)*_0' and 'the image of ⊕_{StP_0} H_R(Pτ̇) equals (H̄^rig)_0' as stated. The repair — take Omega_0 to be a union of fibres of Omega -> Omega_theta — keeps StP_0 finite only when (1 - theta)Omega is finite, which is the hypothesis E1 shows can fail. A second, independent gap sits in the same paragraph. The existence of a finite set A of 5-tuples for which the level-n restriction of the A-compatible families equals the level-n restriction of J(G)^rig_0 is asserted without argument. It needs a Mittag-Leffler / linear-compactness step: the conditions (*) constrain the local distributions on all test functions, not only on those of level I_n. Theorem 23 itself is not refuted: item R16's direct proof avoids both steps ('Avoid ... finite Ω saturation'). But the paper's proof is wrong, and E2's reason cites exactly this truncation as where 'the finiteness needed later is produced'.
findings.evidence: Published proof of Theorem 23, pp. 24-25 (arXiv v3 proof of Theorem 6.3, p. 19, identical): 'Let Ω′ = {τ ∈ Ω; f(P,τ) ≠ 0 for some P} and let Ω0 = ⟨θ⟩·Ω′ be the smallest θ-stable subset of Ω that contains Ω′. Since the action of θ on Ω is of finite order, Ω0 is a finite subset of Ω. ... Let G^rig_0 = {g ∈ G^rig; κ(g) ∈ Ω0} and G^rig_1 = G^rig − G^rig_0. Let J(G)^rig_0 and J(G)^rig_1 be the set of (θ,ω)-invariant distributions supported in G^rig_0 and G^rig_1 ... Then J(G)^rig = J(G)^rig_0 ⊕ J(G)^rig_1, H̄^rig_R = (H̄^rig_R)_0 ⊕ (H̄^rig_R)_1, and J(G)^rig_0 = (H̄^rig_R)^*_0. ... there exists a finite subset A of the 5-tuples (P, τ, Q, γ, x) ... such that J(G)^rig → ⊕ J_P(Pτ̇)|_{H_R(Pτ̇,I_n)} = V|...' The twisted action is ^x f(g) = ω(x) f(x^{-1} g θ(x)) (§1.3, p. 7), so ^h 1_I = ω(h)1_{hIθ(h)^{-1}}. PAPER-HE-18/E2 reason: 'the finiteness needed later is produced by the truncation to a finite θ-stable Ω_0 in the proof of Theorem 23.' E6 addresses only 'the dual argument needs R to be a field'. Item R16 proofSteps: 'Avoid R-dual separation, finite Ω saturation and Howe.'
findings.fix: Add a source issue PAPER-HE-18/E14 (kind error, affects the proof, known new; searched as for E1 plus the sequels arXiv 1611.06825 and 1703.00378). Locator: proof of Theorem 23, p. 25, 'J(G)^rig = J(G)^rig_0 ⊕ J(G)^rig_1, H̄^rig = (H̄^rig)_0 ⊕ (H̄^rig)_1'. Correction: G^rig_0 must be defined by kappa(g) ∈ Omega_0 + (1 - theta)Omega; then StP_0 is finite only if (1 - theta)Omega is finite (cf. E1), and in general the proof is replaced by R16. Reason: the PGL_3 counterexample above. Add E15 (kind gap, affects the proof) for the unargued existence of the finite set A, with the linear-compactness argument as correction (the J_P(Pτ̇) are duals of vector spaces, hence linearly compact, and the conditions (*) are closed). Delete the last sentence of E2's reason, or replace it with a pointer to E14 and R16.

findings.where: PAPER-HE-18/E3 (correction) and its review verdict reason; report section 'The audit of the findings'
findings.claim: E3's correction and the review's confirmation say that a Noetherian coefficient ring restores Theorem 20: 'finite generation of the restriction needs R to be a field (or a Noetherian coefficient ring)', and the review adds 'so the statement as printed needs R noetherian, as the correction records'. The printed statement is a count: J(G(ν))|_{H_R(G,I_n)} 'is generated by N_ν[I : I_n] elements'. Over a Noetherian R the restriction is a submodule of R^{N_ν[I:I_n]}, hence finitely generated, but it need not be generated by N_ν[I:I_n] elements. Counterexample inside the paper's hypotheses. Take R = F_3[x,z]/(xz, z^2), a Noetherian Z[1/2]-algebra; G = Q_2^× with p = 2, θ = id and ω(g) = (1+z)^{v_2(g)} (a unit, since (1+z)^3 = 1, with open kernel). Here Ω = W̃ = Z, every element is minimal, the stratum ν = (0,0) is G(ν) = Z_2^× = I and N_ν = 1. For n = 1, I_1 = 1 + 2Z_2 = I, so ω(I_0) = 1 and [I : I_1] = 1. A (θ,ω)-invariant j satisfies (ω(2) - 1)j(f) = z·j(f) = 0, so j takes values in Ann_R(z). Conversely j_b(f) = b∫_I f is invariant for every b ∈ Ann_R(z). So the restriction of J(G(ν)) to H_R(G,I_1) ∩ H_R(ν) = R·1_I is Ann_R(z) = (x, z), whose minimal number of generators is dim m/m^2 = 2 > 1 = N_ν[I:I_1]. The count in Theorem 20 holds over a field; Noetherianity gives only finite generation, which is what Theorem 18 uses.
findings.evidence: Published Theorem 20, p. 20: 'Then there exists a constant N_ν ∈ N such that for any n ∈ N with ω(I_{n−1}) = 1, J(G(ν))|_{H_R(G,I_n)} is generated by N_ν[I : I_n] elements.' §1.3, p. 7: 'Let R be a commutative Z[1/p]-algebra ... Let ω be a character of G, that is, a homomorphism from G to R^× whose kernel is an open subgroup of G.' §4.2, p. 15: I_n is 'the nth Moy–Prasad subgroup associated to the barycenter'. PAPER-HE-18/E3 correction: 'finite generation of the restriction needs R to be a field (or a Noetherian coefficient ring), and that is the form in which Theorem 18 uses it.' E3 review reason: 'so the statement as printed needs R noetherian, as the correction records.' Computation: in R = F_3[x,z]/(xz,z^2), (a + bz + x g(x))·z = a z, so Ann_R(z) = (x,z) = m, and m/m^2 = F_3x ⊕ F_3z.
findings.fix: Rewrite E3's correction: 'Over an arbitrary R the proof gives only that the restriction is a submodule of a free R-module of rank N_ν[I:I_n]. Over a field the printed bound holds (dimension at most N_ν[I:I_n]). Over a Noetherian R the restriction is finitely generated, but the number N_ν[I:I_n] of generators can fail (R = F_3[x,z]/(xz,z^2), G = Q_2^×).' Append that instance to E3's reason. Correct the review verdict reason in the same way, or record the correction under E3.review as a red-team note. Items F2, F3 and F6 are unaffected: F3 is stated over a field.

findings.claim: Three accepted extractions route the same definition and the same classification theorem to three different owners. The definition: a (θ- or σ-)straight element of the Iwahori–Weyl group, ℓ((wθ)^k) = kℓ(w) for all k. The theorem: He–Nie's classification of straight (twisted) conjugacy classes by (κ, ν̄). HE-18 sends them to the Root-systems Part II; Kisin–Zhou 25 to BunGAndNewtonStrata BG0/BG1; van Hoften 24 to the ADLV Part II of HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas. The σ-twisted case is literally the θ-twisted case with θ = σ acting on W̃. KZ25/N15 and VH24/A09 state the B(G) form: the straight classes biject to B(G). That form is HN14 Theorem 3.3 (HE-18/C7) composed with Kottwitz's classification of B(G) by (κ, ν). HE-18's route reason and ownerAudit screen HE-21, KP18 and KPZ26 but neither KZ25 nor VH24. Its brief ('no second RedMin roadmap') therefore records no coalescence, and neither do the other two. Section 15 requires one owner. The accepted BunGAndNewtonStrata packet (24 September) has no straight-element node, so the KZ25 source route has not been honoured there either. The combinatorial definition and classification can therefore still be given a single owner before any design job runs. (Disclosure: this session's PAPER-FARGUES-SCHOLZE-21 routes B(G), κ and ν to BunGAndNewtonStrata; this finding does not move those.)

findings.where: PAPER-HE-18/H9, H10, H11, H12, H13, N17, F1 in route 7 (SmoothRepresentationsPartIINewtonCocenters); against SmoothRepresentationsCharactersPartII (PAPER-HANSEN-KALETHA-WEINSTEIN-22 route, joined by PAPER-HANSEN-26)
findings.claim: Two Part II roadmaps of the same parent, SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups, both plan the foundations of invariant harmonic analysis on G, and neither names the other. HE-18's NewtonCocenters Part II plans: the conjugation action on C_c(G,R), the commutator submodule and its identification with span{f − ^x f} (Proposition 1), the cocenter H̄ as coinvariants, and invariant distributions J(G) as the dual. SmoothRepresentationsCharactersPartII (HKW22, with HANSEN-26 coalesced into it) plans: coinvariants C_c(G(F)_sr, Λ)_{G(F)} and their orbital-integral description, invariant distributions and trace distributions, the trace Paley–Wiener theorem, and Kazhdan's density theorem. Kazhdan's density theorem includes 'f is a sum of commutators h(x) − h(gxg^{-1})' iff all traces vanish, which is the untwisted case of H11 composed with the cocenter–trace duality. HE-18's route 7 reason distinguishes itself only from SmoothRepresentationsPartIIParahoricCenters. findings.where: PAPER-HE-18/H6 (status missing), H5, L10, the §1.2(a) formula; libraryAudit.declarations entry for TauCeti/NumberTheory/HeckeRing/Basic.lean
findings.claim: The library audit read only lines 1–225 of Tau Ceti's HeckeRing/Basic.lean and classed it as 'Coset/decomposition carriers'. It missed the integral double-coset Hecke ring, which exists at the pins with coefficients in any semiring: Mathlib's IsHeckeTriple and HeckeRing, and Tau Ceti's Shimura multiplicities, convolution product, associativity and ring instance. For a compact open K in a locally profinite G, (K, G) is a Hecke pair, since K ∩ gKg^{-1} has finite index in K. Its Hecke ring 𝕋(G, K; R) is the free R-module on K\G/K with structure constants Shimura's multiplicities. It is H_R(G,K) with its basis {1_{KgK}} (item H6), and convolution is μ(K) times its product, up to the left/right coset convention. The §1.2(a) formula for bi-invariant indicators is that product. Proposition 13 (item L10) is exactly the hypothesis pattern of Tau Ceti's mul_single_single_of_mulMap_eq: every product of representatives lands in the single double coset I_n gg′ I_n, with multiplicity at most one. H6 is therefore not 'missing' in the sense of needing a new carrier: what is missing is the comparison between C_c-convolution at level K and this ring. SR.1, which owns H4–H6, says precisely that the analytic finite-sum convolution must be compared with the library's double-coset multiplication, not duplicated. As written, H6's statement and L10's proof plan a second double-coset multiplication.

findings.claim: E8 and G1 locate the failure of the printed lattice X_*(Z)_{Gal(F̄/F)} in the non-quasi-split case: 'Z = Z_G(A) is not a torus when G is not quasi-split'; 'It must not assume Z is a torus'. The printed formula W̃ ≅ X_*(Z)_{Gal(F̄/F)} ⋊ W_0 is also wrong when Z is a torus. The correct lattice is (X_*(T)_I)^σ, inertia coinvariants followed by Frobenius invariants (Haines–Rapoport Proposition 13 over the strict henselisation, then their Remark 9 descent). This differs from full Galois coinvariants by torsion. Example: G = T = U(1) for the unramified quadratic E/F. Here X_*(T) = Z with σ acting by −1 and inertia trivially, so (X_*(T)_I)^σ = 0 and W̃ = T(F)/T(F)_0 = 0, while X_*(T)_{Gal} = Z/2. So the printed W̃ has two elements where the true one has one, although T is a (quasi-split) torus. The corrections E8 and G1 propose, Λ = Z(F)/Z_0 or transport from F̆ by W̃ ≅ (W̃̆)^σ, are right and cover this case. Only the diagnosis is too narrow: a design job reading 'quasi-split groups are fine' could keep the printed lattice for them.
findings.evidence: Published §1.1, p. 6: 'Set V = X_*(Z)_{Gal(F̄/F)} ⊗ R ... and by [10, Proposition 13], W̃ ≅ X_*(Z)_{Gal(F̄/F)} ⋊ W_0'. Haines–Rapoport (arXiv 0804.3788), setup: 'Let G be a connected reductive group over a strictly henselian discretely valued field L'; Proposition 13: 'W̃ = X_*(T)_I ⋊ W_0'; Remark 9 (Descent): 'Let σ denote an automorphism of L having fixed field L♮ ... W̃^σ = N(L♮)/T(L♮) ∩ T(L)_1 =: W̃(L♮)'. PAPER-HE-18/E8 correction: 'Z = Z_G(A) is not a torus when G is not quasi-split, so X_*(Z) has to be read as the lattice Λ = Z(F)/Z_0 ...'; G1: 'It must not assume Z is a torus'.
findings.fix: Add to E8's reason and to G1: 'The printed lattice is wrong even for tori: Λ = Z(F)/Z_0 ≅ (X_*(T)_I)^σ, which differs from X_*(Z)_{Gal(F̄/F)} by torsion (unramified U(1): 0 against Z/2). V = X_*(Z)_{Gal} ⊗ R is unaffected.' Add the unramified U(1) example as an acceptance test of A2/A8.

findings.claim: A3 marks the barycentric Moy–Prasad filtration planned at RG2.3. Its full content is: I_n, normal in I, θ-stable, cofinal, normalised by the Ω-representatives and their θ-images, with root-depth and toral coordinates. RG2.3 plans parahoric group schemes and says only 'Identify pro-p congruence subgroups and prove their compact openness'. It names neither the Moy–Prasad filtration at a point of the building nor any of A3's stability properties. The two accepted extractions that carry the Moy–Prasad filtration as an item mark it missing and route it to RG2.1–RG2.3 (PAPER-FINTZEN-21/7, PAPER-GAN-HARRIS-SAWIN-ETAL-24/28-moy-prasad). The atlas thus has one planned claim and two missing claims for the same object at the same layer. A3 is already an item of route 3 (the RG2.3 source route), so correcting its status keeps exactly-once routing.
